newsitem.title: GERMANY: Issing-price outlook good, Greenspan warning useful.
newsitem.headline: Issing-price outlook good, Greenspan warning useful.

text.p: Bundesbank chief economist Otmar Issing said on Thursday that the prospects of long-term stability in German prices were extremely favourable.
"We are in a phase of stability in the value of money, which is favourable such as never before," Issing told German television in an interview.

Asked about recent comments from Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan, which triggered a sharp slide in financial markets world-wide, Issing said the remarks had served a useful purpose and had been in the long-term interests of financial markets.
"This was in the interest of markets in the United States, and by extension, in the world as a whole," Issing said.

Commenting on the Bundesbank's decision today to set a money supply growth goal of 3.5 to 6.5 percent for 1997, Issing defended the Bundesbank's monetary targeting strategy even though the target has been missed often in recent years.
He said the fact that the target had been missed would not stop the Bundesbank from convincing the European Central Bank to adopt a similar strategy.
"The exportability of monetary targeting has not been prevented," he said.
Looking at the outlook for the German economy, Issing said the current upturn did not hold price pressures in store.
"We are rather hoping that the upturn will accelerate," he added.
In addition to setting a new money supply target, the Bundesbank on Thursday decided to leave its interest rates unchanged and indicated it had no plans to change policy any time soon.
